title.narrative: Strengthening Development Planning and Management in Greater Cairo (Component 2: Urban Mobility): Capacity Building for Sector Transition

description.narrative:
The construction tender for the BRT is scheduled to be launched in Q2 2023 and the BRT tender operations will be launched approximately 6 months after. UN-Habitat’s role, to date, has included technical assistance and expertise, project coordination, selection of consultants, management of consultant contracts, facilitation among various government entities, and advocacy for the BRT as a viable mode of rapid mass transit. In order to have a mandated institution, within the government, which carries out transportation planning and regulation, the Minister of Housing, Utilities and Urban Communities issued Decree No. 1063 of 2018, called for the establishment of a Transport Regulatory Unit (TRU) to organize public transport in new cities under the authority of New Urban Communities Authority (NUCA), and this was developed through the support of UN-Habitat Egypt office.
The next and crucial phase for the BRT is conducting a public transport transitional study that will focus on providing solutions for existing modes of transport operating on BRT routes. For the BRT to be financially viable, it cannot compete with existing modes of transport. In this respect, a proposed study, which is funded by the development finance institution of the Swedish state, Swedfund International A.B., has been secured to enable the PMU to meet this mandate through the study titled ”Public Transportation Sector Transition Study for 6th of October-Giza BRT Corridor” and providing the necessary support as noted in a request letter from NUCA. This project has accordingly been endorsed by the New Urban Communities Authority (NUCA) and with approval from the Minister of Housing.
The final phase for the BRT includes making sure that non-motorized transport (NMT) elements are incorporated in order to achieve the overarching outcome of having an integrated transportation system. This requires having an in-depth understanding of the existing walking and cycling environment, and the extent to which it provides safe and convenient access for NMT users. Doing so is dependent on having a last-mile access analysis to identify ways of improving NMT elements along the BRT corridor. Based on the above-mentioned expected outputs, there will be a focus on capacity building for the PMU staff, mainly the technical officers and the head of the unit, on project management and other technical skills needed to achieve a fully functioning unit and equipping them with the necessary studies.
This amendment to the existing project document with NUCA was accordingly proposed as an opportunity to enhance the capacity of the BRT project by formalizing current informal public transport modes and integrating them into the BRT operational agency along with the enhancement of last-mile NMT. This amendment also builds on three of the main expected outputs, which entail building the capacities of governmental counterparts in planning for sustainable modes of transportation, tendering for BRT Construction, Operation, and Management, and enhancing the NMT infrastructure in new communities.
